clue.text: Left to, go after 'river bird

indicators.note: the letter for left is told to go after the river, so it is placed at the end

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, and another in East Anglia

explanation.surface: Someone is told to leave the riverside and chase a bird along the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The OUSE is a well-known English river name. An ousel (or ouzel) is an old name for the blackbird or the ring ouzel; the water ouzel is the dipper.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel is a thrush-family songbird, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Gives' rise to opportunities

explanation.surface: Something creates chances for people.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring about something is to cause it; chances to act are suitable times or openings.

clue.text: Medieval room upstairs — that's our system

definitions.meaning: an upper private chamber in a medieval house
the sun's planetary system, the one Earth belongs to

explanation.surface: A guide to an old house points to an upstairs room as the way things are done.
explanation.definitionFit: An upper living room in a medieval house was so called; our planets circle the Sun in its system.

clue.text: Norwegian migrant dying at sea

parts.note: a small Scandinavian rodent famed for mass migrations, said to end in plunging into the sea

explanation.surface: A news report of a Norwegian emigrant perishing on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'migrant' is not a person but the rodent of Scandinavian legend, believed to drown itself en masse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norway rodent migrates in great swarms and popular belief holds that they drown in the sea.

clue.text: Dress is nothing to me — it's boring

parts.note: to dress in something is to wear it
nothing is zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off clothes as tedious: dressing up means nothing to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome and tedious wears you out, so it is dull and boring.

clue.text: Assesses value of aural methods

indicators.note: aural means by ear, so the word for methods is taken as it is spoken

parts.note: methods are ways of doing things

explanation.surface: Someone judges the worth of different ways of listening.
explanation.definitionFit: To measure something's heaviness is to judge its worth, so to assess its value.

clue.text: Product made at an unusual rate — no kidding

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal order, telling us to rearrange

parts.note: no kidding means this is the truth, a fact

explanation.surface: Something manufactured at a surprising speed, honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges RATE into ARTE, then FACT follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is a man-made object, something produced, so a product.

clue.text: Fashionable birds' become doctors one after the other, I hear

parts.note: in means fashionable
terns are seabirds

explanation.surface: Trendy birds take up medicine, one at a time, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one after the other, I hear' is a second hint: it sounds like 'in turns'.
explanation.definitionFit: Junior hospital doctors in training are called by this term in America.

clue.text: He's not even dismissed

parts.note: a number that is not even is odd
he is a man
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: Describes someone who has been sent away, just not evenly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: the one left over when others pair up is unpaired and excluded.
explanation.definitionFit: The one left over after pairing is excluded, a person apart from the rest.

clue.text: Was wrong about rising communist

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word for about is read upwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a red is a communist

explanation.surface: Someone misjudged the rise of a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake, so the past form means made a mistake.

clue.text: Nelson's position with the press ?

parts.note: Nelson stands on top of his famous pillar in Trafalgar Square; a writer with a regular slot in a newspaper occupies a similar named spot

explanation.surface: A question about where Admiral Nelson stood in relation to newspaper reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson's Column is the monument in Trafalgar Square, London. The question mark warns that 'position with the press' means a regular newspaper feature rather than a stance.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist who writes a regular feature has a column in the press, as Nelson has his.

clue.text: Embarrassed, doctor gets 'out of Elizabeth's house

indicators.note: embarrassed letters are put in disarray, so these are mixed up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A red-faced doctor is thrown out of a royal palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embarrassed' looks like it wants RED, but it signals the anagram of DR and OUT. Elizabeth I belonged to the Tudor royal house.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth I was the last monarch of the Tudor dynasty, the royal family that ruled England 1485 to 1603.

clue.text: Frank doesn't get a turn

definitions.meaning: frank means honest, direct and plain-speaking
read literally, something that never turns keeps on going ahead without bending

explanation.surface: A man named Frank is left out when everyone takes turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank means honest and direct; going without a turn means heading on ahead in a line.

clue.text: After Blenheim, the Dutch line has a different family ;tree

definitions.meaning: the Blenheim ... is a famous English apple variety, so this word follows Blenheim in its name
the Dutch royal house is the House of ...-Nassau
a citrus tree belongs to a different botanical family from the apple

explanation.surface: Seems to tell of Dutch royal succession after the battle of Blenheim in 1704.
explanation.walkthrough: Three senses: the Blenheim Orange apple, the Dutch royal House, and the citrus tree, which is of a different family from the apple just mentioned. The battle reading is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch royal dynasty is the House of Orange; an apple variety is the Blenheim Orange; and the citrus tree is no apple.

clue.text: Desires a very quiet and exotic sort of site

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quiet
et is a foreign (Latin or French) 'and'

indicators.note: a sort of word is a version of it, prompting a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Wanting a very peaceful, unusual kind of place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' goes with 'and' to give a foreign 'and', ET; 'sort of' rearranges SITE into ITES.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungers and cravings are longings, so they are desires.

clue.text: Tool for wrestlers would be :'singularly useless

definitions.text: Tool for wrestlers would be :'singularly useless

parts.words: Tool for wrestlers would be :'singularly useless
parts.note: a wrestling leg hold shares its name with a cutting tool whose name is plural, since one blade alone cuts nothing

explanation.surface: A remark that some piece of wrestling equipment is uniquely useless.
explanation.walkthrough: In wrestling the 'scissors' is a hold with the legs. 'Singularly' means both 'remarkably' and 'in the singular': one blade on its own is no use.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting implement with two blades is a tool, and also a wrestling hold, and one half alone cannot cut.

clue.text: They're in no hurry to go south with fishermen

parts.note: trollers are anglers who fish by trailing a line behind a boat

explanation.surface: Relaxed people heading south in company with anglers.
explanation.definitionFit: People who walk leisurely are in no hurry.

clue.text: Bloody kind of road?

definitions.meaning: relating to blood, as in the main vessels carrying it
a main through route for traffic

explanation.surface: Someone curses about what type of road this is.
explanation.definitionFit: Arteries carry blood from the heart; a main traffic route is named after them.

clue.text: Jewel causes Greek poet endless anger

indicators.note: endless says the poet's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Sappho was the lyric poet of Lesbos
ire means anger

explanation.surface: A gem makes an ancient poet furious without end.
explanation.definitionFit: The sapphire is a precious blue gemstone, so it is a jewel.

clue.text: Vet rash to change the yield

indicators.note: the words are told to change, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone warns that a reckless vet will alter the output.
explanation.definitionFit: The crop gathered in is the yield of a season.

clue.text: A bit of money for the speaker

definitions.meaning: read as one who states, a person making a statement

explanation.surface: A coin is handed to whoever is speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient coin of gold or silver was a bit of money; someone who states something speaks.

clue.text: So much French spirit leads to temperamental outburst

parts.note: tant is French for so much
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Too much French liquor leads to a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit of rage or bad temper, as from a child, is an outburst.

clue.text: Is sorry to have lost right to show birds

indicators.note: have lost means a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: regrets means is sorry

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for losing the right to exhibit birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Egrets are white herons, so they are birds.

clue.text: At peak, marshal takes -lower rank as officer of state

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill peak, as on Dartmoor
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals
a general ranks below a field marshal

explanation.surface: At the height of his career, a marshal is demoted to become a minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal' is not a rank here but Napoleon's Marshal NEY; the general's rank is lower than a marshal's. A TOR is a rocky hilltop, common in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief law officer of the Crown is a senior government official, an officer of state.

clue.text: " On the Move"" causes a sensation

parts.note: a stir is a commotion or sensation

explanation.surface: A show called On the Move creates a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up and about and in motion means moving.

clue.text: 18s with spare change

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of the word

explanation.surface: Instructions to swap the 18s for spare ones.
explanation.walkthrough: '18s' refers to 18 down taken as a verb, he or she gathers in crops.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather in a crop is to cut it, so the verb is a synonym of the 18 down answer.

clue.text: The bird with the French name

parts.note: the tit is a small songbird
le is the French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A bird is given its French name.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is what something is called, its name.

clue.text: Drunk beer in it-a bad 'plan

indicators.note: a bad plan is a poorly arranged one, telling us to rearrange the letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Lacing something with beer is judged a poor idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A drunkard is a person who is habitually intoxicated, a drunk.

clue.text: Finds new home-by paying twice?

definitions.meaning: to settle a bill again is to pay it once more

explanation.surface: Someone relocates, apparently by settling the bill twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: To move people to a new place is to rehome them; settling a debt again is paying a second time.

clue.text: Meditates on sources of inspiration

definitions.meaning: the nine goddesses of the arts in Greek myth, or any person who inspires an artist

explanation.surface: Someone thinks hard about where ideas come from.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder is to think deeply; the nine Greek goddesses inspired poets and artists.
